articles.title: Number 83 Bus Services Cancelled Due to High Temperatures
articles.excerpt: The number 83 bus services will be cancelled until after 9pm this evening due to operational issues caused by high temperatures, with ticket acceptance on tram services in place.
articles.content_html:
A bus service in the Rochdale area has been cancelled due to operational issues caused by high temperatures. The number 83 bus services will not operate until after 9pm this evening.

Passengers are advised that there is ticket acceptance on tram services on the Rochdale via Oldham line, which will help them continue their journey during this disruption.

The cancellation of the bus services is expected to affect many commuters and residents relying on this route for travel.

Those planning to use the number 83 service are encouraged to check for updates and consider alternative travel options.

articles.title: Woman arrested on suspicion of murder after 31-year-old man dies in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: A 37-year-old woman has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a 31-year-old man died at an address in Rochdale.
articles.content_html:
A murder investigation has been launched after a 31-year-old man died at an address in Rochdale.

Emergency services were called to a property on Great Howarth shortly before 7.40pm on Tuesday 11 August. A man was found unresponsive inside the address. Paramedics attempted to save him, but he was pronounced dead a short time later.

A 37-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of murder as officers began enquiries into the circumstances surrounding the death. An arrest is not a finding of guilt, and the investigation remains at an early stage.

Police have not released the man's identity in the information currently available to Rochdale Daily. Further details about the circumstances of his death, including any subsequent charging decision or release from custody, should be treated as unconfirmed unless formally announced by investigators.

The case concerns an address on Great Howarth in Rochdale. Rochdale Daily will update this report when further verified information becomes available.

articles.content_html:

Transport for Greater Manchester has apologised for any inconvenience caused by the lift's unavailability. Passengers are advised to check the Transport for Greater Manchester website for more information.

articles.title: Action Together Achieves Volunteer Centre Quality Accreditation in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Action Together has been awarded the Volunteer Centre Quality Accreditation, recognising its commitment to volunteering in Rochdale, alongside Oldham and Tameside.
articles.content_html:
Action Together has announced it has achieved the Volunteer Centre Quality Accreditation (VCQA) from NAVCA, marking a significant milestone for its operations in Rochdale. This accreditation is a re-award for the organisation in Oldham and Tameside, but it is the first time Action Together has been recognised for its work in Rochdale.

The VCQA award, which complements the Local Infrastructure Quality Accreditation (LIQA), highlights Action Together's commitment to quality and impact as a Local Infrastructure Organisation. The organisation exceeded three of the five criteria assessed, which include good practice development, developing volunteer opportunities, and the voice of volunteering, while meeting the remaining two categories of strategic development of volunteering and brokerage.

Feedback from the assessment praised Action Together for its embedded organisational and equality, diversity, and inclusion strategies in volunteering work. The organisation was noted for its high-quality training and development support, flexibility in responding to the needs of volunteers, and effective partnership working within the community.

NAVCA gathered feedback from various organisations and partners during the assessment, with comments highlighting Action Together's visibility and integration within the community. One volunteer-involving organisation remarked that Action Together is well embedded in the local landscape and the voluntary sector.

articles.title: Burnley Man Banned from Keeping Animals After Dog Found Emaciated in Rochdale Home
articles.excerpt: A man has received a 15-year ban on keeping animals after an emaciated dog was discovered in a Rochdale property. Paul Lewis Dawson was sentenced at Tameside Magistrates' Court for animal welfare offences.
articles.content_html:
A man has been banned from keeping animals for 15 years after an emaciated dog was found living in unsanitary conditions at a property in Rochdale. Paul Lewis Dawson, 37, of Brownside Road in Burnley, pleaded guilty to three offences under the Animal Welfare Act 2006 at Tameside Magistrates' Court on 31 July.

The RSPCA began investigating on 6 August 2025 after receiving reports about a bullbreed dog named Kano being left unattended at a property on Alice Street in Rochdale. RSPCA inspector Beth Fazackerley and animal rescue officer Francesca Iraci attended the address, where they observed Kano through the keyhole and noted he appeared very skinny. After no one answered the door, they pushed wet dog food through the letterbox, which Kano ate.

Later that evening, the RSPCA returned with a police officer after obtaining a warrant. Upon entering the property, Kano was found to be in poor condition, having difficulty standing and displaying visible signs of distress. The dog was covered in fleas, had wounds on his body, and was suffering from severe weight loss and anaemia due to an insufficient diet. Rubbish and faeces were found throughout the property, creating an unsuitable living environment for the animal.

Dawson received a 22-week prison sentence, suspended for 12 months, and was ordered to complete 18 Rehabilitation Activity Requirement days and 80 hours of unpaid work, in addition to paying £400 in costs. The judge described the case as "the most serious case of animal cruelty I have ever dealt with." Kano has since been taken into the care of the RSPCA and has recovered.
